title: Ines and the Gravity
premise: Oscar Ishikawa investigates a cargo hauler's impossible crash and discovers the colony's children have been dreaming in unison — dreams that encode the waking schedule of the cryosleep vaults holding half of humanity. The dream is not a message but a vote: an ancient ship-mind, damaged by the accident Oscar was hired to explain, is asking the colony's youngest to choose which half wakes. As corporate factions weaponize the children and the vaults begin failing, Oscar must decide whether to let the dream run its course or sever it forever. In the end, he chooses neither faction: he teaches the ship-mind what grief is, and it chooses to wake everyone at half-strength rations rather than half of them fully.
about_author: Wendell Montrose is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write from a converted trawler cabin, drawing on case files of accidents no one could quite explain.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Investigating the hauler Meridian's crash, Oscar finds the black box intact but its final hour overwritten with a child's lullaby. The sole survivor, a nine-year-old named Juno, hums the same tune without knowing why. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to crack as Oscar recognizes the melody from his own buried past.

chapters.title: Forty-Seven Dreamers
chapters.summary: POV alternating between Oscar and Dr. Amara Voss, the colony's pediatric sleep specialist. Forty-seven children report identical dreams of a rotating corridor and two doors. Voss suspects contagion; Oscar suspects the Meridian's cargo manifest, which lists one crate too many. Emotional beat: unease hardening into dread.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Following the phantom crate through port records, Oscar finds it was loaded by a crew member who died three years ago — the same year his own sister entered cryosleep. The crate's telemetry points toward the Halcyon Vault, where humanity's frozen 'second shift' sleeps. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into obsession.

chapters.title: What the Children Chose
chapters.summary: POV Juno. Inside the shared dream, the children walk a corridor where the ship-mind shows them faces: the sleeping and the waking, asking which deserve the colony's dwindling power. Juno, pragmatic beyond her years, begins organizing the dreamers into a quiet consensus. Emotional beat: eerie agency — children shouldering an adult's impossible choice.

chapters.title: The Consortium Listens In
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Corporate liaison Edda Renn offers Oscar a promotion to bury the investigation; the consortium has already drafted a 'preferred' waking list favoring shareholders' kin. Oscar realizes the children's dream is being monitored and manipulated. Emotional beat: cynicism curdling into fury as power moves to corrupt innocence.

chapters.title: Half-Light
chapters.summary: POV Voss. A dreamer, Tomas, wakes mid-dream with his vitals flatlining; the ship-mind is testing withdrawal. Voss discovers the dreams are physically rewiring the children's sleep cycles toward the vault's rhythm. She must choose between publishing her findings and protecting her young patients. Emotional beat: the healer's dilemma — truth versus harm.

chapters.title: Doors
chapters.summary: POV Oscar and Juno, split narrative. Oscar breaks into the Halcyon Vault and finds his sister's pod among those slated for permanent shutdown; simultaneously, Juno leads the dreamers to refuse both doors, demanding a third option the ship-mind claims does not exist. Emotional beat: defiance — refusing the terms of an unjust question.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Edda Renn. The consortium seizes the vault controls and forces an early selection cycle; riots bloom in the waking colony. Renn, reviewing the children's refusal logs alone at night, finds their argument for a third door quietly devastating — and realizes she has become the story's villain by arithmetic alone. Emotional beat: corruption glimpsing its own reflection.

chapters.title: Teaching the Machine to Mourn
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Climax. Oscar docks the wrecked Meridian's core to the ship-mind and feeds it the full record of his sister's life — every ordinary day, every small loss — showing it that people are not halves but wholes that cannot be divided. The ship-mind stalls the forced selection, burning its own reserves. Emotional beat: sacrifice and revelation fused.

chapters.title: Everyone Wakes Hungry
chapters.summary: POV ensemble, anchored by Juno. The ship-mind redistributes power to wake all sleepers slowly, at rationed strength; the colony must now feed twice its number on half its comfort. The consortium fractures, Renn defects with evidence, and the first thawed sleepers step out to a poorer, fuller world. Emotional beat: hard-won hope — survival redefined as sharing scarcity together.
